name: MonarchStackedBarChart
title: StackedBarChart
wrapsNative: MonarchBarChart (Swift Charts BarMark with yStart/yEnd stacking, chartXSelection / chartYSelection, an AXChartDescriptor) with layout .stacked by default and the 100% offset computed before drawing; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend
summary: Stacked bars showing how each category's total splits into parts, as values or as shares of 100%, vertical or horizontal, with totals, inspection, legend toggles, drill-in and the data as a table.
whenToUse: To show a total per period or category and what it is made of, such as tickets by status per month, or to compare the mix across categories regardless of their size with offset .expand.
whenNotToUse: For one series per category use MonarchBarChart, or MonarchBarList for a ranked list. For a single whole use MonarchStackedProportionBar or MonarchDonutChart. For parts over a continuous time axis use a Swift Charts AreaMark in MonarchChartFrame.
api: init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchBarChartSeries], description: String? = nil, categoryTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, orientation: MonarchBarChartOrientation = .vertical, layout: MonarchBarChartLayout = .stacked, offset: MonarchStackedBarChartOffset = .normal, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, highlightedIndex: Int? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchBarChartReferenceLine] = [], valueRange: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsValueLabels: Bool = false, isLegendToggleable: Bool = true, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchStackedBarChartLabels = MonarchStackedBarChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchStackedBarChartLabels.init(bar: MonarchBarChartLabels = MonarchBarChartLabels(), shareSeries: String? = nil)
MonarchBarChartSeries.init(_ key: String, label: String, values: [Double?], color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchBarChartReferenceLine.init(_ value: Double, label: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's accessibility label.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app.

options.name: series
options.description: The parts, each with a key, a label, one value per category and an optional colour slot. The first series sits on the baseline.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table and the name of VoiceOver's category axis.

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure; the name of VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: vertical columns or horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: stacked (one bar of parts per category) or grouped (the parts side by side).

options.name: offset
options.description: normal stacks the values; expand stacks each category's shares so every bar is 100% long. Only applies when stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready with no categories or no series shows empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Without it the chart keeps its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise; the bars of the others are dimmed.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines at a value. Not drawn with the 100% offset.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. With the 100% offset the axis is always 0...1 (0% to 100%).

options.name: showsValueLabels
options.description: Writes each stack's total at its end (each bar's value when grouped). With the 100% offset the total is 100%.

options.name: isLegendToggleable
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240 points for columns; 32 points per category, at least 120, for bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the bar chart's (frame, category, total, no data, details, clear) and the share summary sentence.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values with the normal offset. With the 100% offset values are percentages in the environment's locale, with at most one decimal.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index (an index into the app's categories, also with the 100% offset) from Details or from the category's VoiceOver action.

states.name: ready
states.description: The stacked plot, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: 100% offset
states.description: Every bar is 100% long; the value axis, value labels, inspection row, table and summary show percentages. Reference lines are not drawn.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a touch or drag: the category's band is shaded and a row under the plot reads every part and the stack's total, with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the other categories' bars are drawn at reduced opacity.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The part leaves the bars and the others keep their colours. With the 100% offset the others keep their shares, so the bar ends short of 100%. The table still lists it.

states.name: grouped
states.description: With layout .grouped the parts stand side by side and the offset is ignored.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's muted placeholder of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: As MonarchBarChart: parts take the theme's data slots 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text colour; the grid uses the subtle border colour, the zero line the strong border colour, labels the muted text colour and the inspected band the muted background. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web's StackedBarChart is its BarChart with stacking on and the 100% offset; the iOS component is the same composition over MonarchBarChart (Swift Charts). The web separates stacked parts with a hairline in the surface colour; MonarchBarChart has no option for a separator between parts, so iOS parts touch (a request to add one to MonarchBarChart is recorded). With the 100% offset the web formats axis ticks with no decimals and other values with one; iOS uses one formatter with at most one decimal for both. Inspection uses touch selection and a row under the plot rather than a hover tooltip; there is no keyboard arrow navigation. Android ships the same MonarchStackedBarChart. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The plot is one accessibility element labelled with the title. Its value is the generated summary or the summary parameter: with values, MonarchBarChart's summary (categories, then each shown series' total and highest category); with the 100% offset, the categories, then each shown series' average share and largest share.
The plot carries MonarchBarChart's AXChartDescriptor, with a Total series when stacked; with the 100% offset the values are shares and are read as percentages.
With onSelect, the plot has one VoiceOver custom action per category, named "Details, <category>".
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a switch that is on while its series is shown; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value, and a Total column when stacked, as text.
Parts are told apart by the legend's names, the inspection row and the table, not by colour alone.
edgeCases: With the 100% offset, negative values count as zero and a category whose positive total is zero has zero shares everywhere.
Shares are computed over every series, hidden ones included, so hiding a part leaves a gap instead of rescaling the others.
Gaps (nil) and values that are not finite draw nothing and are written "No value" in the inspection row and "–" in the table.
In the values offset, negative parts stack down from zero separately from the positive parts.
More than five series: the sixth and later are neutral.
Touch inspection and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the share logic and summary are unit-tested.

examples.title: Stacked with totals
examples.template:
MonarchStackedBarChart(
    {{title}},
    categories: [{{categories.0}}, {{categories.1}}, {{categories.2}}, {{categories.3}}, {{categories.4}}, {{categories.5}}],
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries({{series.0.key}}, label: {{series.0.label}}, values: [{{series.0.values.0}}, {{series.0.values.1}}, {{series.0.values.2}}, {{series.0.values.3}}, {{series.0.values.4}}, {{series.0.values.5}}]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries({{series.1.key}}, label: {{series.1.label}}, values: [{{series.1.values.0}}, {{series.1.values.1}}, {{series.1.values.2}}, {{series.1.values.3}}, {{series.1.values.4}}, {{series.1.values.5}}]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries({{series.2.key}}, label: {{series.2.label}}, values: [{{series.2.values.0}}, {{series.2.values.1}}, {{series.2.values.2}}, {{series.2.values.3}}, {{series.2.values.4}}, {{series.2.values.5}}]),
    ],
    description: {{description}},
    categoryTitle: {{categoryLabel}},
    showsValueLabels: true
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
examples.code:
MonarchStackedBarChart(
    "Tickets by status",
    categories: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"],
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries("resolved", label: "Resolved", values: [120, 132, 101, 134, 190, 230]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("pending", label: "Pending", values: [22, 18, 30, 25, 19, 21]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("escalated", label: "Escalated", values: [8, 6, 12, 9, 7, 5]),
    ],
    description: "First half of the year",
    categoryTitle: "Month",
    showsValueLabels: true
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-US"))

examples.title: Horizontal, 100%, with drill-in
examples.setup:
@State private var opened: String?
private let teams = ["Platform", "Design systems", "Growth"]
examples.code:
MonarchStackedBarChart(
    "Work by status",
    categories: teams,
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries("done", label: "Done", values: [34, 21, 12]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("review", label: "In review", values: [6, 9, 3]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("todo", label: "To do", values: [10, 4, 18], color: .neutral),
    ],
    categoryTitle: "Team",
    orientation: .horizontal,
    offset: .expand,
    onSelect: { opened = teams[$0] }
)

examples.title: Grouped
examples.code:
MonarchStackedBarChart(
    "Tickets by status",
    categories: ["Apr", "May", "Jun"],
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries("resolved", label: "Resolved", values: [134, 190, 230]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("pending", label: "Pending", values: [25, 19, 21]),
    ],
    layout: .grouped,
    height: 200
)
